searchText: Some more questions about 7702: Has implications to ASE (Address Space Extension) been analyzed? Are there any restrictions or logic related to the length of `address` being sent via a Set Code Tx and stored in the `0xef01 ++ address` format? I.e. what happens if that `address` is 19 or 32 bytes long If so, this would be good to include in the rationale of the EIP. empty blob list is not valid in 4844, so maybe makes sense to not allow it here too For code accessing opcodes, I guess both direct target and delegate become warm? I think the cleanest approach would be to require in the transaction that the address field in each authorization_list tuple to have exactly 20 bytes, which is what the destination field requires in types 0-3. This should be spelled out in the EIP. And then in post-ASE (and potentially post-Verkle) world you switch the requirement to be 32 bytes and rely on `codesize` to discriminate between 20- and 32-byte designations? If this works then what you wrote seems enough (and indeed cleanest) for now.
